subject: maths
question: A buyer ordered 12 kg of premium sugar and some standard sugar. The price of premium sugar per kg was three times that of the standard sugar. Due to an ordering error, the quantities of the two types of sugar were interchanged. This decreased the total cost by 25%. Find the ratio of the quantity of premium sugar to standard sugar in the original order.
solution:
**Given:**

Premium sugar price = 3 × Standard sugar price

Premium quantity = 12 kg

Standard quantity = x kg

Quantities interchanged → Total cost ↓ by 25%

**Formula used:**

Total cost change = (Original − New) ÷ Original

**Calculations:**

Price of premium = 3p, price of standard = p

⇒ Original cost = 12 × 3p + x × p = 36p + xp

⇒ New cost (interchanged) = 12 × p + x × 3p = 12p + 3xp

⇒ Decrease = 25% of original

⇒ (36p + xp) − (12p + 3xp) = 25% of (36p + xp)

⇒ 36p + xp − 12p − 3xp = (1/4)(36p + xp)

⇒ (24p − 2xp) = (1/4)(36p + xp)

⇒ 96p − 8xp = 36p + xp

⇒ 60p = 9xp

⇒ x = 60 ÷ 9 = 20/3

⇒ Premium : Standard = 12 : 20/3

⇒ = 36 : 20

⇒ = 9 : 5

**∴ Required ratio = 9 : 5.**
